I read all 380 commits and the 127-row PR sheet. Here is what I found.

## The signal-to-noise split

| Type | Commits | User-visible? |
|---|---|---|
| chore | 153 | No |
| refactor | 73 | Mostly no — 2 exceptions below |
| test | 64 | No |
| ci | 33 | No |
| fix | 26 | Yes |
| docs | 20 | No |
| perf | 10 | Yes |
| feat | 1 | Yes |

37 commits carry user-visible change. They collapse to about 14 distinct facts, because the same fix landed in 2 to 4 modules under separate commits. For example, "guard the null cursor in the paginator" landed four times: `api`, `db`, `queue`, and `webhooks`. That is one fact for a reader, not four.

## Three things hide in the refactors

These carry a `refactor:` prefix, but they change the public surface. Verify each against the diff before you publish.

1. **`stop re-exporting the internal error types`** — 8 commits across `core`, `db`, `auth`, `billing`, and `jobs`. If any consumer imports those error classes today, the import breaks.
2. **`refactor(api): drop the unused v1 export route`** (`56dc828`, PR #4152) — the subject says "unused". The diff touches `src/api/router.js`, `src/api/handlers.js`, and `test/api.test.js`. A removed HTTP route is breaking for anyone who calls it.
3. **`fix(auth): return 401 for an expired token instead of 403`** (`1d2bd55`) — a status-code change. A client that branches on 403 breaks. It carries a `fix:` prefix, but it belongs under Breaking.

## Dependency bumps

16 distinct bumps, all patch or minor. Nine are runtime dependencies: `fastify`, `pg`, `knex`, `ioredis`, `pino`, `undici`, `zod`, `nanoid`, `dotenv`. Seven are build or test tooling. No major version. Nothing here needs a changelog line.

## Draft entry

```markdown
## 4.2.0 — 2026-08-28

### Breaking
- The package no longer re-exports the internal error types. Import them from
  the public entry point instead.
- The v1 export route is removed.
- An expired token now returns 401. It returned 403 before.

### Added
- Failed webhook deliveries retry with exponential backoff.

### Fixed
- The HTTP client clears its timer when the socket drops.
- The HTTP client closes the pool on shutdown.
- Outgoing requests no longer carry a duplicate header.
- The paginator no longer fails on a null cursor.
- An empty allowlist no longer causes an error.
- A URL keeps one trailing slash, not two.
- The database layer no longer logs the whole request body.
- The latency histogram reports the correct units.
- The trace id survives a retry.
- The token parser reports what is wrong in the error message.
```

Two notes on the draft:

The `feat(webhooks)` commit (`395fb48`) also touches `src/core/config.js`. It likely adds a config option for the backoff. Check the diff. If the option exists, name it in the Added line.

The 10 `perf` commits have no heading in your template. They cover four themes: skip a JSON round-trip on the hot path, batch the metric writes, avoid a clone in the mapper, and reuse the parsed schema between requests. I left them out to keep the three headings. If you want them, one line under Added works: "Lower request latency on the hot path."

## Open questions

- **Minimum Node version.** Six `docs: note the minimum node version` commits and four `ci: run the suite on node 22` commits appear. I cannot tell from the log whether the supported floor moved. If it moved, that is a Breaking line. Check `.nvmrc` and the `engines` field.
- **Source disagreement.** The PR sheet covers 127 rows against 380 commits, and it omits the `undici` bumps entirely. I treated `commits.log` as authoritative. The sheet also lists duplicate rows with the same title under different authors, for example #4120 and #4121.

Tell me which of the three breaking items you confirm, and I will write the entry into `CHANGELOG.md`.
